name: like-inverted
why: NARROW: inverts LIKE's verdict. Only scenarios whose predicate uses cmp.like reach it -- 236 of 8150 by feature vector -- so a same-size random subset can plausibly miss it. This is the row that tests the SELECTION rather than the subset size

name: sort-nulls-placement
why: BROAD: inverts NULLS FIRST/LAST in the executor's in-memory sort; changes row ORDER only, so a multiset-only assertion is blind to it

name: sort-direction
why: BROAD: inverts ASC/DESC in the executor's in-memory sort; the broadest ordering defect available

name: is-null-inverted
why: BROAD: IS NULL returns FALSE for NULL and TRUE otherwise; changes which rows QUALIFY

name: is-not-null-inverted
why: BROAD: the IS NOT NULL twin of the above; a corpus can cover one spelling and not the other
